root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional panels on click events within its own module. Keyboard navigation changes the checked state via arrow keys, firing a change event but not a click. Moreover, the opt-out radio is in a separate module, so its change event does not propagate to the first module, leaving the conditional panel visible.
repair_strategy: Make each radios module listen for change events on the containing form (or document) for radios sharing the same name. When such a change occurs, update all conditional panels in that module. This ensures conditionals stay in sync regardless of which radio in the group is selected, and regardless of input method.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all radio options in the same group (including across modules) using arrow keys, and conditional fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Multiple modules on the same form will each attach a change listener; this is safe as they only react to their own radio group name.
If a module contains radios with different names, the behavior may be incorrect, but the component assumes a single group per module.
The change event fires on every radio change, but setAttributes is idempotent.
verification_requirements: Selecting 'Text message' via ArrowDown shows the mobile number field.
Moving to 'I do not want reminders' via another ArrowDown hides the mobile number field.
Clicking radios with mouse continues to work as before.
Form data reflects the correct selected value after keyboard navigation.
Rapid keyboard navigation does not cause stale states.
